simple.meaning: פָּכָה (pâkâh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to pour.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Ezekiel, beginning at Ezekiel 47:2. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פָּכָה (H6379) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: פָּכָה (pâkâh) / H6379 is traced through Ezekiel 47:2 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H6379. pakah מָּכָה verb Pi`el trickle , perhaps denominative; — Participle plural מִן מְפַכִּים מַיִם Ezek 47:2 water trickling on the south side.

occurrences.englishText: Then he brought me out by the way of the gate northward, and led me around by the way outside to the outer gate, by the way of the gate that looks toward the east. Behold, waters ran out on the right side.
